candidate.title: Chia-PET
candidate.scope: The assigned middle Chia-PET row of the supplied Illumina poster crop, expanded there as Chromatin interaction analysis by paired-end tag sequencing (ChIA-PET). This is a single, original linker/MmeI-based schematic: fragmented protein-associated chromatin is immunoenriched, linked by proximity ligation, and converted to paired-end-tag DNA. Chia-PET and ChIA-PET are capitalization variants of the same target name. The visible ChIPmentation row above and Hi-C/3-C/Capture-C row below are neighboring workflows, not depicted alternatives for this card. The catalogue also discusses advanced/long-read ChIA-PET, but that Tn5-based adaptation is not drawn on the assigned route. The endpoint is a PET DNA product; sequencing and downstream analysis are interpreted through its information content without inventing unshown operations.

states.label: Chromatin with protein-associated DNA regions
features: The input icons show gray nucleosomes and two DNA regions brought together at a blue protein/protein-complex symbol. Colors distinguish regions schematically, not chemical formulas.

Primary-supported preparation history: cross-linked chromatin. The row contains no separately captioned cross-linking step; the two left-hand chromatin icons are context and prepared input, not two processing branches.

states.label: Oligonucleotide DNA half-linkers
features: Incorporated DNA reagent established by the primary source, not a separate incoming branch drawn in the poster.
MmeI restriction sites define the PET extraction interface; the original implementation uses distinguishable A/B linker barcodes to assess some nonspecific ligations.
The generic yellow connector does not depict the separately labeled aliquots of the original implementation; these remain internal details of the broad ligation block.

evidence.quote: DNA fragments in ChIP complexes were then ligated to biotinylated half-linkers (linker ligation) containing flanking MmeI restriction sites. The complexes were further ligated under dilute conditions (proximity ligation). Paired-End Tags (PETs) were extracted from the ligation products by MmeI digestion.
This full-length linker is derived from ligation of two half-linkers, A or B, each with a unique barcode nucleotide (CG for half-linker A and AT for half-linker B).

Hence, we classified the PETs with linker AB as the chimeric PET dataset, and the PETs with linkers AA and BB as non-chimeric PET dataset (note that the PETs with linkers AA and BB may still have certain chimeric PETs).

states.label: Linker-connected DNA fragments within the enriched complex
features: The ligation icon shows the red and teal DNA segments joined at one side through a yellow connector while the blue protein complex is still present.

Primary-supported molecular interpretation: DNA half-linkers and proximity ligation form a linker-connected DNA product with MmeI sites. The yellow connector is a generic schematic junction, not a resolved chemical structure.

states.label: Paired-end-tag DNA product
features: The digestion region shows a central yellow connector between colored DNA segments and small separated peripheral pieces; the final DNA icon is a shorter teal/red line with no separately visible yellow block.

Primary-supported endpoint: a 20 bp genomic head tag and a 20 bp genomic tail tag remain joined by a 38 bp linker after MmeI extraction. The disappearance of the yellow symbol at the endpoint does not establish physical linker removal.

The readout carrier is genomic DNA plus the synthetic DNA linker. Paired tag origins report an enriched fragment or a candidate association of two protein-associated genomic loci; the protein itself is not sequenced.
This is the schematic PET DNA endpoint. The primary source describes sequencing-adapter addition and amplification downstream, which the poster does not resolve into operations.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate

operations.label: Ligation
operations.description: The broad Ligation block incorporates oligonucleotide DNA linkers and joins fragment ends held near one another in an enriched complex. The source-resolved implementation includes linker attachment and proximity ligation within this one captioned block; no split-aliquot branches are drawn.
operations.mechanism: DNA half-linkers carrying MmeI sites are attached to chromatin-fragment ends, followed by proximity ligation to form full linker connections. The diagram preserves a protein-associated intermediate at this boundary.
operations.information_effect: Converts proximity of fragment ends into a physical DNA linkage. Inter-ligation can preserve a candidate contact between different fragments; the primary method also produces self-ligation products and random chimeric ligations. Linker barcode composition assesses part of that background and does not prove all retained pairs are biological contacts.

Hence, we classified the PETs with linker AB as the chimeric PET dataset, and the PETs with linkers AA and BB as non-chimeric PET dataset (note that the PETs with linkers AA and BB may still have certain chimeric PETs).
ChIA-PET proximity ligation generates two types of ligation products: self-ligation of the same DNA fragments and inter-ligation between different DNA fragments.

operations.label: Restriction enzyme digestion
operations.description: This schematic transition takes linker-connected chromatin to released PET DNA and separated peripheral DNA pieces. MmeI extraction retains the short genomic tags flanking the linker while leaving bulk flanking DNA outside the PET. The disappearance of protein is compressed into the drawing: the primary source reverses cross-links and purifies DNA before MmeI digestion; restriction cleavage alone is not assigned protein removal.
operations.mechanism: Primary-resolved interface: reversal of cross-links and DNA purification precede MmeI cleavage at the linker-flanking extraction sites. Only Restriction enzyme digestion is captioned in the poster, so this remains one broad schematic operation.
operations.information_effect: Retains the pairing of two genomic end tags in a tag-linker-tag DNA carrier while removing surrounding DNA context. Paired-end tag mapping can distinguish single-fragment self-ligation from candidate inter-fragment contacts and locate their genomic origins. Contact interpretation remains conditional on selection, ligation background and tag mappability; it is not a direct measurement of protein sequence or proof of a functional regulatory interaction.
